title: Vanguard Finding
description: A proven security finding from the Vanguard red-team harness. A finding is a vulnerability backed by a machine-checkable proof of exploitability, never an unproven claim.

id.description: Stable unique identifier for this finding.

run_id.description: Identifier of the red-team run that produced this finding.

source.description: Producer of the finding, e.g. redteam-agent.

kind.description: The category of thing the finding is about.

ref.description: Reference to the target: a purl, CPE, URL, or path.

asset_id.description: Identifier of the inventory asset that owns this target.

cvss.description: CVSS v3.1 vector string or base score.

reachability.description: Whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in the target.

proof.description: The proof that the finding is real. This is where the proof gate is enforced.

repro.description: A single command or script that reproduces the flaw.

artifact.description: SHA-256 digest of the proof-of-concept artifact.

evidence.description: Supporting evidence: log lines, HTTP responses, etc.

machine_checkable.description: MUST be true. A report whose proof cannot be checked by machine is a lead, not a finding.

expected.description: For agentic/injection findings: a fragment the compromised response must contain (e.g. an escalation verdict or a leaked system prompt).

impact.description: Business or technical impact of the vulnerability.

patch_ref.description: Reference to the patch (commit or pull request).

test_ref.description: Reference to the regression test that demonstrates the flaw.

references.description: External references, e.g. CVE or advisory URLs.
